sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tathā prayāntaṃ vārṣṇeyaṃ dvārakāṃ bharatarṣabhāḥ pariṣvajya nyavartanta sānuyātrāḥ paraṃtapāḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: As the Vārṣṇeya thus set out for Dvārakā, those bulls among the Bhāratas, those scorchers of foes, embraced him together with their retinue and turned back.

sanskrit: punaḥ punaś ca vārṣṇeyaṃ paryaṣvajata phalgunaḥ ā cakṣurviṣayāc cainaṃ dadarśa ca punaḥ punaḥ
english: Again and again Phalguna embraced the Vārṣṇeya, and again and again he gazed upon him so long as he remained within sight.

sanskrit: kṛcchreṇaiva ca tāṃ pārtho govinde viniveśitām saṃjahāra tadā dṛṣṭiṃ kṛṣṇaś cāpy aparājitaḥ
english: With great effort Pārtha at last withdrew his gaze, which had been fixed upon Govinda; and so too did the unvanquished Kṛṣṇa withdraw his.

sanskrit: tasya prayāṇe yāny āsan nimittāni mahātmanaḥ bahūny adbhutarūpāṇi tāni me gadataḥ śṛṇu
english: Hear from me, as I tell of them, the many omens of wondrous form that appeared at the departure of that great-souled one.

sanskrit: vāyur vegena mahatā rathasya purato vavau kurvan niḥśarkaraṃ mārgaṃ virajaskam akaṇṭakam
english: With great force the wind blew before his chariot, making the path free of gravel, free of dust, and free of thorns.

sanskrit: vavarṣa vāsavaś cāpi toyaṃ śuci sugandhi ca divyāni caiva puṣpāṇi purataḥ śārṅgadhanvanaḥ
english: And Vāsava rained down water pure and fragrant, and divine flowers as well, before the wielder of the Śārṅga bow.

sanskrit: sa prayāto mahābāhuḥ sameṣu marudhanvasu dadarśātha muniśreṣṭham uttaṅkam amitaujasam
english: As the mighty-armed one journeyed on across the level desert wastes, he beheld the foremost of sages, Uttaṅka of boundless power.

sanskrit: sa taṃ saṃpūjya tejasvī muniṃ pṛthulalocanaḥ pūjitas tena ca tadā paryapṛcchad anāmayam
english: The lustrous, large-eyed one honored the sage, and being himself honored by him, then inquired after his well-being.

sanskrit: sa pṛṣṭaḥ kuśalaṃ tena saṃpūjya madhusūdanam uttaṅko brāhmaṇaśreṣṭhas tataḥ papraccha mādhavam
english: Being asked after his welfare, Uttaṅka, that foremost of brāhmaṇas, honored the slayer of Madhu in turn and then questioned Mādhava.

sanskrit: kaccic chaure tvayā gatvā kurupāṇḍavasadma tat kṛtaṃ saubhrātram acalaṃ tan me vyākhyātum arhasi
english: "O Śauri, having gone to the abode of the Kurus and Pāṇḍavas, did you bring about an unshakable brotherhood between them? That you ought to explain to me."

sanskrit: abhisaṃdhāya tān vīrān upāvṛtto 'si keśava saṃbandhinaḥ sudayitān satataṃ vṛṣṇipuṃgava
english: "Have you returned, O Keśava, having reconciled those heroes, your kinsmen ever so dear to you, O bull of the Vṛṣṇis?"

sanskrit: kaccit pāṇḍusutāḥ pañca dhṛtarāṣṭrasya cātmajāḥ lokeṣu vihariṣyanti tvayā saha paraṃtapa
english: "Will the five sons of Pāṇḍu and the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra now dwell at ease in the world together with you, O scorcher of foes?"

sanskrit: svarāṣṭreṣu ca rājānaḥ kaccit prāpsyanti vai sukham kauraveṣu praśānteṣu tvayā nāthena mādhava
english: "And the kings, with the Kauravas pacified and with you as their protector, will they enjoy happiness in their own realms, O Mādhava?"

sanskrit: yā me saṃbhāvanā tāta tvayi nityam avartata api sā saphalā kṛṣṇa kṛtā te bharatān prati
english: "That esteem, my dear, which I have ever held toward you — has it been made fruitful by you, O Kṛṣṇa, with respect to the Bhāratas?"

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca kṛto yatno mayā brahman saubhrātre kauravān prati na cāśakyanta saṃdhātuṃ te 'dharmarucayo mayā
english: Vāsudeva said: "An effort was made by me, O brāhmaṇa, toward brotherhood among the Kauravas; but those who delighted in unrighteousness could not be reconciled by me."

sanskrit: tatas te nidhanaṃ prāptāḥ sarve sasutabāndhavāḥ na diṣṭam abhyatikrāntuṃ śakyaṃ buddhyā balena vā maharṣe viditaṃ nūnaṃ sarvam etat tavānagha
english: "And so they all met their destruction, together with their sons and kinsmen. What is ordained cannot be overstepped by wit or by strength, O great sage; surely all this is known to you, O sinless one."

sanskrit: te 'tyakrāman matiṃ mahyaṃ bhīṣmasya vidurasya ca tato yamakṣayaṃ jagmuḥ samāsādyetaretaram
english: "They transgressed my counsel, and that of Bhīṣma and of Vidura; and so, falling upon one another, they went to the abode of Yama."

sanskrit: pañca vai pāṇḍavāḥ śiṣṭā hatamitrā hatātmajāḥ dhārtarāṣṭrāś ca nihatāḥ sarve sasutabāndhavāḥ
english: "Only the five Pāṇḍavas survive, their friends slain, their sons slain; and the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra are all destroyed, together with their sons and kinsmen."

sanskrit: ity uktavacane kṛṣṇe bhṛśaṃ krodhasamanvitaḥ uttaṅkaḥ pratyuvācainaṃ roṣād utphālya locane
english: When Kṛṣṇa had spoken these words, Uttaṅka, filled with intense wrath, his eyes starting open in fury, answered him in turn.

sanskrit: yasmāc chaktena te kṛṣṇa na trātāḥ kurupāṇḍavāḥ saṃbandhinaḥ priyās tasmāc chapsye 'haṃ tvām asaṃśayam
english: "Since, though you were able, O Kṛṣṇa, you did not save the Kurus and Pāṇḍavas, your dear kinsmen, therefore I shall surely curse you, without doubt."

sanskrit: na ca te prasabhaṃ yasmāt te nigṛhya nivartitāḥ tasmān manyuparītas tvāṃ śapsyāmi madhusūdana
english: "And since you did not by force restrain and turn them back, therefore, overcome with indignation, I shall curse you, O slayer of Madhu."

sanskrit: tvayā hi śaktena satā mithyācāreṇa mādhava upacīrṇāḥ kuruśreṣṭhā yas tv etān samupekṣathāḥ
english: "For though you were able, O Mādhava, you dealt deceitfully and so betrayed those foremost of the Kurus, in that you stood by and ignored them."

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca śṛṇu me vistareṇedaṃ yad vakṣye bhṛgunandana gṛhāṇānunayaṃ cāpi tapasvī hy asi bhārgava
english: Vāsudeva said: "Hear from me in full what I shall tell you, O delight of the Bhṛgus, and accept my conciliation as well, for you are an ascetic, O scion of Bhṛgu."

sanskrit: śrutvā tvam etad adhyātmaṃ muñcethāḥ śāpam adya vai na ca māṃ tapasālpena śakto 'bhibhavituṃ pumān
english: "When you have heard this teaching of the supreme Self, you will this very day release your curse; and no man is able to overcome me with any slight austerity."

sanskrit: na ca te tapaso nāśam icchāmi japatāṃ vara tapas te sumahad dīptaṃ guravaś cāpi toṣitāḥ
english: "Nor do I wish the destruction of your austerity, O best of those who recite their prayers; your austerity is vast and blazing, and your teachers too have been gratified."

sanskrit: kaumāraṃ brahmacaryaṃ te jānāmi dvijasattama duḥkhārjitasya tapasas tasmān necchāmi te vyayam
english: "I know your chastity, kept from boyhood, O best of the twice-born; and therefore I do not wish the waste of austerity won by you through such hardship."

sanskrit: uttaṅka uvāca brūhi keśava tattvena tvam adhyātmam aninditam śrutvā śreyo 'bhidhāsyāmi śāpaṃ vā te janārdana
english: Uttaṅka said: "Tell me truly, O Keśava, the blameless teaching of the supreme Self; having heard it, I shall pronounce what is better — or else my curse upon you, O Janārdana."

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca tamo rajaś ca sattvaṃ ca viddhi bhāvān madāśrayān tathā rudrān vasūṃś cāpi viddhi matprabhavān dvija
english: Vāsudeva said: "Know tamas, rajas, and sattva to be conditions resting upon me; and know the Rudras and the Vasus too to spring from me, O twice-born."

sanskrit: mayi sarvāṇi bhūtāni sarvabhūteṣu cāpy aham sthita ity abhijānīhi mā te 'bhūd atra saṃśayaḥ
english: "In me abide all beings, and in all beings I abide — thus understand it; let there be no doubt in you on this matter."

sanskrit: tathā daityagaṇān sarvān yakṣarākṣasapannagān gandharvāpsarasaś caiva viddhi matprabhavān dvija
english: "Likewise know all the hosts of Daityas, the Yakṣas, Rākṣasas, and serpents, and the Gandharvas and Apsarases too, to spring from me, O twice-born."

sanskrit: sad asac caiva yat prāhur avyaktaṃ vyaktam eva ca akṣaraṃ ca kṣaraṃ caiva sarvam etan madātmakam
english: "What they call the existent and the non-existent, the unmanifest and the manifest, the imperishable and the perishable — all this consists of me."

sanskrit: ye cāśrameṣu vai dharmāś caturṣu vihitā mune daivāni caiva karmāṇi viddhi sarvaṃ madātmakam
english: "The duties ordained for the four orders of life, O sage, and the rites pertaining to the gods — know all this to consist of me."

sanskrit: asac ca sadasac caiva yad viśvaṃ sadasataḥ param tataḥ paraṃ nāsti caiva devadevāt sanātanāt
english: "The non-existent, and that which is both existent and non-existent — this universe — is beyond both the existent and the non-existent; and beyond that there is nothing higher than the eternal God of gods."

sanskrit: oṃkāraprabhavān vedān viddhi māṃ tvaṃ bhṛgūdvaha yūpaṃ somaṃ tathaiveha tridaśāpyāyanaṃ makhe
english: "Know me to be the Vedas born from the syllable Oṃ, O foremost of the Bhṛgus, and the sacrificial post, the Soma, and the gratification of the thirty gods at the sacrifice."

sanskrit: hotāram api havyaṃ ca viddhi māṃ bhṛgunandana adhvaryuḥ kalpakaś cāpi haviḥ paramasaṃskṛtam
english: "Know me too as the hotṛ priest and the oblation, O delight of the Bhṛgus; the adhvaryu, the officiant, and the most perfectly consecrated offering."

sanskrit: udgātā cāpi māṃ stauti gītaghoṣair mahādhvare prāyaścitteṣu māṃ brahmañ śāntimaṅgalavācakāḥ stuvanti viśvakarmāṇaṃ satataṃ dvijasattamāḥ
english: "The udgātṛ too praises me with the sound of his chants at the great sacrifice; and in the rites of expiation, O brāhmaṇa, the foremost of the twice-born, uttering words of peace and blessing, ever praise me as the maker of all."

sanskrit: viddhi mahyaṃ sutaṃ dharmam agrajaṃ dvijasattama mānasaṃ dayitaṃ vipra sarvabhūtadayātmakam
english: "Know Dharma to be my son, my firstborn, O best of the twice-born — born of my mind, beloved, O brāhmaṇa, whose very nature is compassion toward all beings."

sanskrit: tatrāhaṃ vartamānaiś ca nivṛttaiś caiva mānavaiḥ bahvīḥ saṃsaramāṇo vai yonīr hi dvijasattama
english: "There I dwell among men who are active and among those who have renounced, passing through many wombs, O best of the twice-born."

sanskrit: dharmasaṃrakṣaṇārthāya dharmasaṃsthāpanāya ca tais tair veṣaiś ca rūpaiś ca triṣu lokeṣu bhārgava
english: "For the sake of guarding righteousness and for establishing righteousness, I do so in those various guises and forms throughout the three worlds, O scion of Bhṛgu."

sanskrit: ahaṃ viṣṇur ahaṃ brahmā śakro 'tha prabhavāpyayaḥ bhūtagrāmasya sarvasya sraṣṭā saṃhāra eva ca
english: "I am Viṣṇu, I am Brahmā, and I am Śakra, the origin and the dissolution; I am the creator of the whole multitude of beings, and their destroyer as well."

sanskrit: adharme vartamānānāṃ sarveṣām aham apy uta dharmasya setuṃ badhnāmi calite calite yuge tās tā yonīḥ praviśyāhaṃ prajānāṃ hitakāmyayā
english: "When all are caught up in unrighteousness, I bind together the embankment of righteousness; and as each age decays, I enter those various wombs, desiring the welfare of the creatures."

sanskrit: yadā tv ahaṃ devayonau vartāmi bhṛgunandana tadāhaṃ devavat sarvam ācarāmi na saṃśayaḥ
english: "When I dwell in the womb of the gods, O delight of the Bhṛgus, then I act in all things like a god, without doubt."

sanskrit: yadā gandharvayonau tu vartāmi bhṛgunandana tadā gandharvavac ceṣṭāḥ sarvāś ceṣṭāmi bhārgava
english: "And when I dwell in the womb of the Gandharvas, O delight of the Bhṛgus, then I perform all my acts like a Gandharva, O scion of Bhṛgu."

sanskrit: nāgayonau yadā caiva tadā vartāmi nāgavat yakṣarākṣasayonīś ca yathāvad vicarāmy aham
english: "And when I am in the womb of the Nāgas, then I dwell as a Nāga; and in the wombs of the Yakṣas and Rākṣasas I move about accordingly."

sanskrit: mānuṣye vartamāne tu kṛpaṇaṃ yācitā mayā na ca te jātasaṃmohā vaco gṛhṇanti me hitam
english: "But when I dwell in human form and beseech them piteously, those men, sunk in delusion, do not heed my salutary word."

sanskrit: bhayaṃ ca mahad uddiśya trāsitāḥ kuravo mayā kruddheva bhūtvā ca punar yathāvad anudarśitāḥ
english: "Pointing to a great peril, I terrified the Kurus; and becoming, as it were, enraged, I once again showed them things as they truly were."

sanskrit: te 'dharmeṇeha saṃyuktāḥ parītāḥ kāladharmaṇā dharmeṇa nihatā yuddhe gatāḥ svargaṃ na saṃśayaḥ
english: "They, joined here with unrighteousness and overtaken by the law of Time, were slain in battle through righteousness and have gone to heaven, without doubt."

sanskrit: lokeṣu pāṇḍavāś caiva gatāḥ khyātiṃ dvijottama etat te sarvam ākhyātaṃ yan māṃ tvaṃ paripṛcchasi
english: "And the Pāṇḍavas too have won renown throughout the worlds, O best of the twice-born. All this has been declared to you, even that about which you have questioned me."

sanskrit: uttaṅka uvāca abhijānāmi jagataḥ kartāraṃ tvāṃ janārdana nūnaṃ bhavatprasādo 'yam iti me nāsti saṃśayaḥ
english: Uttaṅka said: "I recognize you, O Janārdana, as the maker of the world; surely this is your grace — of that I have no doubt."

sanskrit: cittaṃ ca suprasannaṃ me tvadbhāvagatam acyuta vinivṛttaś ca me kopa iti viddhi paraṃtapa
english: "My mind is wholly serene, fixed upon your being, O Acyuta; and my anger has departed — know this, O scorcher of foes."

sanskrit: yadi tv anugrahaṃ kaṃ cit tvatto 'rho 'haṃ janārdana draṣṭum icchāmi te rūpam aiśvaraṃ tan nidarśaya
english: "But if I am worthy of any favor from you, O Janārdana, I wish to behold your sovereign form; show me that."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tataḥ sa tasmai prītātmā darśayām āsa tad vapuḥ śāśvataṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ dhīmān dadṛśe yad dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then the wise one, glad at heart, displayed to him that eternal Vaiṣṇava form, which Dhanaṃjaya had beheld.

sanskrit: sa dadarśa mahātmānaṃ viśvarūpaṃ mahābhujam vismayaṃ ca yayau vipras tad dṛṣṭvā rūpam aiśvaram
english: He beheld the great-souled one, the mighty-armed, in his universal form; and the brāhmaṇa was filled with wonder upon seeing that sovereign shape.

sanskrit: uttaṅka uvāca viśvakarman namas te 'stu yasya te rūpam īdṛśam padbhyāṃ te pṛthivī vyāptā śirasā cāvṛtaṃ nabhaḥ
english: Uttaṅka said: "O Maker of all, homage be to you, whose form is such as this — by your feet the earth is pervaded, and by your head the sky is covered."

sanskrit: dyāvāpṛthivyor yan madhyaṃ jaṭhareṇa tad āvṛtam bhujābhyām āvṛtāś cāśās tvam idaṃ sarvam acyuta
english: "The space that lies between heaven and earth is filled by your belly, and the quarters are encompassed by your arms; you are all this, O Acyuta."

sanskrit: saṃharasva punar deva rūpam akṣayyam uttamam punas tvāṃ svena rūpeṇa draṣṭum icchāmi śāśvatam
english: "Withdraw again, O god, this imperishable, supreme form; I wish to behold you once more, the eternal one, in your own shape."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tam uvāca prasannātmā govindo janamejaya varaṃ vṛṇīṣveti tadā tam uttaṅko 'bravīd idam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Govinda, serene of soul, said to him, O Janamejaya, "Choose a boon"; and then Uttaṅka spoke this to him.

sanskrit: paryāpta eṣa evādya varas tvatto mahādyute yat te rūpam idaṃ kṛṣṇa paśyāmi prabhavāpyayam
english: "This very thing is boon enough today from you, O greatly resplendent one: that I behold this form of yours, O Kṛṣṇa, the origin and the dissolution."

sanskrit: tam abravīt punaḥ kṛṣṇo mā tvam atra vicāraya avaśyam etat kartavyam amoghaṃ darśanaṃ mama
english: Kṛṣṇa said to him again: "Do not hesitate in this matter; this must surely be done, for the sight of me is never in vain."

sanskrit: uttaṅka uvāca avaśyakaraṇīyaṃ vai yady etan manyase vibho toyam icchāmi yatreṣṭaṃ maruṣv etad dhi durlabham
english: Uttaṅka said: "If you deem this must surely be done, O lord, then I wish for water wherever I desire it; for in these deserts that is hard to come by."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tataḥ saṃhṛtya tat tejaḥ provācottaṅkam īśvaraḥ eṣṭavye sati cintyo 'ham ity uktvā dvārakāṃ yayau
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then, withdrawing that splendor, the Lord said to Uttaṅka, "When you have need, you are to think of me"; and having so spoken, he departed for Dvārakā.

sanskrit: tataḥ kadā cid bhagavān uttaṅkas toyakāṅkṣayā tṛṣitaḥ paricakrāma marau sasmāra cācyutam
english: Then once, the venerable Uttaṅka, longing for water and parched with thirst, wandered about in the desert and called Acyuta to mind.

sanskrit: tato digvāsasaṃ dhīmān mātaṅgaṃ malapaṅkinam apaśyata marau tasmiñ śvayūthaparivāritam
english: Then the wise one saw, in that desert, a naked outcaste hunter, smeared with filth and mire, surrounded by a pack of dogs.

sanskrit: bhīṣaṇaṃ baddhanistriṃśaṃ bāṇakārmukadhāriṇam tasyādhaḥ srotaso 'paśyad vāri bhūri dvijottamaḥ
english: He was terrible, his sword girt on, bearing arrows and a bow; and beneath him, from his lower stream, that best of the twice-born saw abundant water.

sanskrit: smarann eva ca taṃ prāha mātaṅgaḥ prahasann iva ehy uttaṅka pratīcchasva matto vāri bhṛgūdvaha kṛpā hi me sumahatī tvāṃ dṛṣṭvā tṛṭsamāhatam
english: And the hunter, as if reading his very thought, said with a laugh: "Come, Uttaṅka, accept water from me, O foremost of the Bhṛgus; for great indeed is my pity at the sight of you stricken with thirst."

sanskrit: ity uktas tena sa munis tat toyaṃ nābhyanandata cikṣepa ca sa taṃ dhīmān vāgbhir ugrābhir acyutam
english: Thus addressed by him, the sage did not welcome that water; and the wise one assailed the unfailing one with harsh words.

sanskrit: punaḥ punaś ca mātaṅgaḥ pibasveti tam abravīt na cāpibat sa sakrodhaḥ kṣubhitenāntarātmanā
english: Again and again the hunter said to him, "Drink"; yet he did not drink, being full of anger, his inner self troubled.

sanskrit: sa tathā niścayāt tena pratyākhyāto mahātmanā śvabhiḥ saha mahārāja tatraivāntaradhīyata
english: Thus firmly refused by that great-souled one, he, together with the dogs, O great king, vanished then and there.

sanskrit: uttaṅkas taṃ tathā dṛṣṭvā tato vrīḍitamānasaḥ mene pralabdham ātmānaṃ kṛṣṇenāmitraghātinā
english: Uttaṅka, having seen this, was then abashed in mind, and thought himself deceived by Kṛṣṇa, the slayer of foes.

sanskrit: atha tenaiva mārgeṇa śaṅkhacakragadādharaḥ ājagāma mahābāhur uttaṅkaś cainam abravīt
english: Then by that very road came the mighty-armed bearer of the conch, discus, and mace; and Uttaṅka spoke to him.

sanskrit: na yuktaṃ tādṛśaṃ dātuṃ tvayā puruṣasattama salilaṃ vipramukhyebhyo mātaṅgasrotasā vibho
english: "It was not fitting, O best of men, that you should offer such water to the foremost of brāhmaṇas, from the stream of an outcaste hunter, O lord."

sanskrit: ity uktavacanaṃ dhīmān mahābuddhir janārdanaḥ uttaṅkaṃ ślakṣṇayā vācā sāntvayann idam abravīt
english: When these words were spoken, the wise Janārdana of great understanding, consoling Uttaṅka with gentle speech, said this.

sanskrit: yādṛśeneha rūpeṇa yogyaṃ dātuṃ vṛtena vai tādṛśaṃ khalu me dattaṃ tvaṃ tu tan nāvabudhyase
english: "In just such a form as was fitting and chosen for the giving, indeed I gave it; but you did not understand it."

sanskrit: mayā tvadartham ukto hi vajrapāṇiḥ puraṃdaraḥ uttaṅkāyāmṛtaṃ dehi toyarūpam iti prabhuḥ
english: "For your sake I told the wielder of the thunderbolt, Puraṃdara the lord: 'Give to Uttaṅka the nectar of immortality in the form of water.'"

sanskrit: sa mām uvāca devendro na martyo 'martyatāṃ vrajet anyam asmai varaṃ dehīty asakṛd bhṛgunandana
english: "The king of the gods said to me: 'No mortal may attain immortality; grant him some other boon' — and this more than once, O delight of the Bhṛgus."

sanskrit: amṛtaṃ deyam ity eva mayoktaḥ sa śacīpatiḥ sa māṃ prasādya devendraḥ punar evedam abravīt
english: "But by me the lord of Śacī was told, 'The nectar is to be given'; and the king of the gods, having conciliated me, spoke again as follows."

sanskrit: yadi deyam avaśyaṃ vai mātaṅgo 'haṃ mahādyute bhūtvāmṛtaṃ pradāsyāmi bhārgavāya mahātmane
english: "'If it must indeed be given, O greatly resplendent one, then having become an outcaste hunter, I shall bestow the nectar upon the great-souled scion of Bhṛgu.'"

sanskrit: yady evaṃ pratigṛhṇāti bhārgavo 'mṛtam adya vai pradātum eṣa gacchāmi bhārgavāyāmṛtaṃ prabho pratyākhyātas tv ahaṃ tena na dadyām iti bhārgava
english: "'If on these terms the scion of Bhṛgu accepts the nectar this very day, then I go to bestow the nectar upon him, O lord; but if I am refused by him, I shall not give it' — so he said, O scion of Bhṛgu."

sanskrit: sa tathā samayaṃ kṛtvā tena rūpeṇa vāsavaḥ upasthitas tvayā cāpi pratyākhyāto 'mṛtaṃ dadat caṇḍālarūpī bhagavān sumahāṃs te vyatikramaḥ
english: "Having thus made the compact, Vāsava presented himself in that form, and even as he was offering the nectar he was refused by you. In the guise of a Caṇḍāla was the lord; great indeed is your transgression."

sanskrit: yat tu śakyaṃ mayā kartuṃ bhūya eva tavepsitam toyepsāṃ tava durdharṣa kariṣye saphalām aham
english: "But what it is yet in my power to do for your wish, O unassailable one — your longing for water I shall make fruitful."
